research_notes:
CATL's largest single-site battery base, in Fuding, Ningde, Fujian, China. Wholly owned by CATL (not a JV). Phase 1 (RMB 17bn) started production December 2021 as a 60 GWh lithium-ion base; four cell factories (No.1-No.4) plus module factories were reported in production by September 2022. Total planned capacity across the base widely reported at 120 GWh (five factory buildings); nameplate_capacity_gwh set to 120 and capacity_by_year_json shows the 60->120 GWh ramp. In May 2026 CATL announced a sixth-phase expansion adding 40 GWh of annual sodium-ion cell capacity (RMB 5bn / ~$735m), which would bring the base's total planned capacity to 149 GWh; that sodium-ion expansion is under construction (~24-month build, targeting ~2028) and is not yet operational, so it is not counted in the operational nameplate here. The overall site is operational (lithium-ion lines running since 2021/2022). Precise plant coordinates not confirmed by a source, so latitude/longitude left null (site is in Fuding, Fujian). Sources: CnEVPost (2021-12-22) on 120 GWh planned / production start; CnEVPost (2026-05-09) and Battery-News (2026-05-11) on the 40 GWh sodium-ion phase-six expansion to 149 GWh total.

plant_name: CATL Shanghai Lingang battery base (Nanhui New City)
research_notes:
The candidate "CATL Nanhui New City plant" is identified as CATL's Shanghai Lingang battery base, located in the Lin-gang Special Area of the China (Shanghai) Pilot Free Trade Zone, which sits within Nanhui New City (南汇新城), Pudong, Shanghai — about 3 km from Tesla Giga Shanghai. It is CATL's 6th of 13 global production bases (address cited as 168 Xinsipinglu Road, Lingang New Area). Announced June 2021 (Reuters, via electrive/InsideEVs) as an 80 GWh plant. IMPORTANT NUANCE: an initial leased site near Giga Shanghai did only battery MODULE assembly from cells shipped in, but the purpose-built Lingang base manufactures CELLS under one roof; CATL delivered first LFP cells to Tesla Giga Shanghai in Jan 2022 (electrive, 2022-01-08). Chemistry is LFP for Tesla standard-range vehicles. Wholly owned by CATL, not a JV. The 80 GWh figure was described as an unconfirmed target/rumour at announcement, so capacity confidence is moderate and the full-nameplate reference year could not be confirmed (left null). Precise coordinates not sourced (Lingang/Nanhui area only), left null. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CATL (lists Lingang as an operational base); electrive.com/2021/08/19 (announcement, 80 GWh); electrive.com/2022/01/08 (first LFP cells to Tesla); insideevs.com/news/559587 (Shanghai plant supplies Tesla).
